category_title: High-ability students who resist training and rely on rereading for memorization
minimal_context: The student is examining the learning objectives for her modular math course and writing down which resources she will use to study.
dialogue:
TUTOR: For this task, please examine the learning objectives for our math module and describe in writing which resources you will use to study.

STUDENT: I looked at the modules, but I'm not going to study differently. I already use many of the tactics presented in the training.

TUTOR: Please write down the specific strategies you plan to use for these objectives.

STUDENT: I'm just going to read the textbook chapters again. Like I wrote down, rereading and spacing can help me better memorize the material.

TUTOR: What do you think about trying some of the other new strategies we discussed instead of just rereading?

STUDENT: I'm not changing how I study. It's not going to make a difference anyway because everyone knows I am just dumb.

options.A: Maintain a ratio of praise to correction at 3:1 or 4:1 during the math module sessions.
options.B: Provide a model answer in the form of a sample student's plan, drawing attention to all available resources.
options.C: Incorporate frequent opportunities for the student to respond (OTRs) during the math module instruction.
options.D: Allow the student to select a reinforcer to be earned contingent upon demonstrating desired study behaviors.
